claims.text: Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is controlled primarily by the composition-dependent Gibbs free-energy difference between BCC and FCC.
The high Cr and Al contents of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 reduce ΔG_bcc-fcc below a critical threshold.
Reducing ΔG_bcc-fcc below the proposed threshold allows BCC to remain metastable over a broad thermal regime.
Thermal processing can increase ΔG_bcc-fcc beyond the critical threshold.
Crossing the proposed ΔG_bcc-fcc threshold initiates transformation toward FCC.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be synthesized with a high-temperature BCC microstructure.
Varying annealing temperature and cooling rate modulates the thermodynamic driving force for phase transformation.
High Cr and Al contents induce lattice distortions and distinctive local chemical environments in this alloy.
The proposed Cr- and Al-induced lattice distortions and local environments modify interfacial energies.
Changes in interfacial energy effectively tune the bulk ΔG_bcc-fcc.
Mixing enthalpy and configurational entropy set ΔG_bcc-fcc in the alloy.
A sufficiently low ΔG_bcc-fcc prevents FCC from becoming thermodynamically favorable during cooling.
Slower cooling or higher annealing temperatures elevate ΔG_bcc-fcc.
Once the thermodynamic driving force exceeds kinetic barriers, Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 partially or completely converts to FCC.
Rapid quenching or optimized annealing maintains low ΔG_bcc-fcc and preserves BCC at lower temperatures.
Thermal treatments producing higher ΔG_bcc-fcc cause measurable FCC formation.
Under standard cooling conditions, the control sample has a marginally stable BCC phase.
Diffusion is not too sluggish above approximately 600 °C for the proposed mechanism to operate.
The proposed mechanism applies only when phase segregation or precipitation does not occur.

contradictions.description: The BCC phase is called metastable when ΔG_bcc-fcc is low, but the mechanism also says that this condition prevents FCC from becoming thermodynamically favorable. If FCC is not thermodynamically favored, describing BCC as metastable is inconsistent unless another lower-free-energy phase is specified.

Cooling rate is treated as changing or maintaining the intrinsic Gibbs free-energy difference, even though at fixed temperature and composition cooling rate ordinarily changes kinetic access rather than the equilibrium bulk ΔG. No processing-induced compositional change is specified to reconcile this.

The alloy is described as BCC at high temperature, while higher annealing temperatures are proposed to elevate ΔG_bcc-fcc and promote FCC. The stated temperature dependence is therefore internally ambiguous and potentially opposite to the asserted high-temperature BCC state.

The experiment and predictions extend down to room temperature, but the hypothesis is said to apply only approximately above 600 °C. It is unclear whether retained room-temperature BCC/FCC fractions are claimed as mechanistic outcomes or merely frozen records of transformations above the boundary.
